title: Hell
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Hell is the conscious judgment and eternal punishment of the wicked who remain outside Christ. Scripture describes it as final condemnation, eternal punishment, torment, the second death, and the lake of fire.
summary: Hell is the conscious judgment and eternal punishment of the wicked who remain outside Christ. Scripture describes it as final condemnation, eternal punishment, torment, the second death, and the lake of fire.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the only Savior from the judgment to come. His warnings about hell are truthful and merciful, calling sinners to repent and come to Him for life, forgiveness, and deliverance from eternal condemnation.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Hell is real because God is holy, sin is serious, judgment is certain, and rejecting Christ has eternal consequences. Scripture does not present hell as a temporary inconvenience or a symbolic scare tactic.

Jesus Himself warned about hell with soberness and clarity. In Luke 16, the rich man is conscious after death, in anguish, and unable to cross into comfort.

Hell is also connected to the final judgment. Revelation describes the lake of fire as the second death, where those not found written in the book of life are cast.

This doctrine must be taught with tears, reverence, and truth. Hell should never be used for entertainment, manipulation, pride, or harshness. But it must not be softened into something less than Scripture teaches.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
If hell is denied or minimized, the urgency of the Gospel is weakened. People need to know what Christ saves sinners from.

This doctrine also confronts false comfort. It is not loving to hide eternal danger from people. Love tells the truth and points to the Savior.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Take eternal judgment seriously and flee to Christ. Do not treat hell lightly, joke about it, soften it beyond Scripture, or speak of it with pride. Warn with tears, preach Christ with hope, and remember that salvation is found only in the One who rescues sinners from the wrath to come.
